label: Iron
name: Fe
job: Helps your red blood cells carry oxygen from your lungs to every part of your body.
powers: Carries oxygen in your red blood cells (as hemoglobin)
Stores oxygen in your muscles
Supports energy, growth and brain development
Helps make some hormones
fun: Your body has no real way to get rid of extra iron, except through bleeding. That's why it controls absorption so tightly, and why megadoses are a bad idea.
formsIntro: Food has two kinds of iron, and supplements come in several forms.
forms: Found in meat, fish and poultry. Your body absorbs it best.
Found in plants and fortified foods. Absorbed less, but vitamin C at the same meal helps.
Common supplement forms. Labels list the elemental iron, which is what counts.

label: Calcium
name: Ca
job: Builds strong bones and teeth, and helps your muscles, heart and nerves work.
powers: Builds and maintains bones and teeth
Helps muscles contract, including your heart
Helps nerves send signals
Helps blood clot
low: Tingling in the hands, feet or around the mouth (if blood calcium drops)
fun: Your blood calcium stays almost perfectly steady. If you don't eat enough, your body quietly borrows it from your bones.
formsIntro: Calcium in food is easy. Supplements mostly come in two forms.
forms: Dairy, fortified foods, calcium-set tofu, sardines and some greens.
About 40% calcium. Cheaper, but take it with food. Can cause gas or constipation.
About 21% calcium. Works without food and is gentler on the stomach.

label: Magnesium
name: Mg
job: Keeps your muscles and nerves working, and helps control blood sugar and blood pressure.
powers: Helps hundreds of enzymes do their jobs
Keeps muscles and nerves working
Helps control blood sugar and blood pressure
Helps build bone, protein and DNA
fun: Magnesium sits at the center of chlorophyll, the green pigment in plants. Leafy greens are literally built around it.
formsIntro: Food is the easy route. Supplement forms differ in how well they're absorbed.
forms: Seeds, nuts, beans, whole grains and greens.
Absorbed better than oxide or sulfate in small studies.
Absorbed less, and more likely to cause diarrhea. Also used as laxatives and antacids.

label: Zinc
name: Zn
job: Supports your immune system, helps wounds heal, and keeps your sense of taste and smell working.
powers: Supports your immune system
Helps wounds heal
Keeps taste and smell working
Helps make proteins and DNA
fun: Three ounces of oysters have more than two days' worth of zinc.
formsIntro: Zinc in food comes with protein. Supplements come in several salts.
forms: Seafood, meat, dairy, seeds, beans and whole grains.
Other supplement forms. Labels list elemental zinc.

label: Iodine
name: I
job: Lets your thyroid make the hormones that set how your body uses energy.
powers: Lets your thyroid make thyroid hormones
Those hormones set your metabolism
Needed for a baby's brain and bone development
low: Swelling at the front of the neck (goiter)
Tiredness, feeling cold or weight gain (an underactive thyroid)
fun: The US started iodizing table salt in the 1920s to fight goiter. Manufacturers still do it, though it's voluntary.
formsIntro: Iodine comes from salt, dairy and seafood, and supplements use one main form.
forms: Iodized salt, dairy, eggs and seafood. Seaweed varies hugely.
The form recommended in prenatal supplements.
Iodine content varies widely, so they're hard to dose safely.

label: Selenium
name: Se
job: Helps protect your cells from damage and helps your thyroid hormones work.
powers: Part of enzymes that protect cells from damage
Helps your thyroid hormones work
Helps make DNA
Supports reproduction and immunity
low: Rarely causes symptoms on its own
Can worsen thyroid problems when iodine is also low
Linked to a rare heart muscle disease in very low-selenium regions
fun: Too much selenium has a giveaway sign: breath that smells like garlic.
formsIntro: Selenium in food is mostly bound to protein. Supplements use a few forms.
forms: The main form in grains, beans and nuts. Also used in supplements.

label: Omega-3
name: ALA, EPA & DHA
job: Healthy fats that build your cell membranes, especially in the brain and eyes, and support your heart.
powers: Build cell membranes, especially in the brain and eyes
EPA and DHA lower triglycerides (a blood fat)
Support a baby's brain and eye development
Help make signals for your heart, blood vessels and immune system
fun: DHA is concentrated in your retina and brain, and breast milk naturally contains it.
formsIntro: There are three main omega-3s. Only ALA is strictly essential, because your body makes just a little EPA and DHA from it.
forms: From plants: flaxseed, chia, walnuts, canola and soybean oil.
From fish and seafood. These are the ones linked to heart benefits.
Supplement sources. Algae oil is a vegan source of EPA and DHA.
